purpose: Pins Gate E's pass/fail criteria BEFORE the E2 report (#52) or gallery (#53) exist, so the review (#54) cannot rationalize whatever the numbers turn out to be. The E2 notebook imports this file; it does not define thresholds inline.
committed_before: The corpus, the E2 report (#52), and the gallery (#53). Any change to a threshold here after those exist must be a separate, dated commit that justifies itself.

failure_classes.defect: The corpus does not faithfully implement its own committed inputs (selection list, n_h table, centroids). The design is UNTESTED because the artifact is wrong. Consequence: fix code, re-run E1/E2, STAY IN THIS MAP. Not a Gate E verdict.
failure_classes.finding: The corpus faithfully implements the design, and the DESIGN is revealed wrong. Consequence: record the verdict, STOP this map, open a fresh map with the implicated knob (map Destination + Out-of-scope).

attrition_contract_branch.note: Several count criteria have two variants keyed on issue #50 (the materialization attrition contract), which was open when this bar was written. #50's answer does not set thresholds; it selects which pre-committed branch is live. The notebook reads the live contract from corpus_meta.json.

E2.1a_metric_fidelity.test: For every materialized window, the manifest's frozen-metric values equal the catalog's values for the same window_id.
E2.1a_metric_fidelity.tolerance: exact under the manifest's declared storage dtype; the cast (if the manifest stores float32 vs the catalog's float64) is documented in the #48 schema, and equality is checked after that documented cast
E2.1a_metric_fidelity.rationale: This is the only part of E2.1 that carries Phase E information: did E1 write the rows it was told to write. A mismatch is a mis-join/mis-order/recompute bug, not a knob.

backfill_to_budget.test: materialized set == selected set by construction; nothing to test beyond E2.2b.

accept_shortfall.test: The dropped windows are metric-indistinguishable from retained windows: per-metric Wasserstein-1 distance between dropped and retained (within the frozen vector) below the pre-registered bound.
accept_shortfall.threshold: SET BLIND when #50 lands on accept_shortfall — pending #50's 'measure first' result. Random attrition is harmless; terrain-correlated attrition is bias.

E2.1b_drop_selectivity.rationale: Under backfill this is tautological. Under shortfall the question is not how many dropped (E2.2) but whether the drops were metric-selective.

E2.1c_pool_ecdf.test: Per-metric ECDF overlay, corpus vs 3,052,735-row kept pool, with Wasserstein-1 distances printed as descriptive labels. Second overlay weights each tile by N_h/n_h (should approximately recover the pool).
E2.1c_pool_ecdf.explicitly_never_a_gate: The corpus is deliberately terrain-diverse, NOT pool-representative (Neyman grants the rarest stratum a 1.8x per-row premium, #42; FSCS spreads within-stratum). 'Matches the pool' is the WRONG success criterion. Published to give the E3 honesty note a number instead of an adjective. No threshold attached.

E2.2a_selection_integrity.test: The selection list AS THE DRIVER LOADED IT matches Phase D's commit.

checks.per_stratum_counts: equal to every n_h row in d2-allocation-nh.json

E2.2a_selection_integrity.rationale: Catches the dull failure nobody plans for: a stale file or rows dropped on parse. Independent of every other decision; costs milliseconds.

backfill_to_budget.test: realized per-stratum counts == n_h exactly; total == 50000

accept_shortfall.test: realized <= selected for every stratum; realized > selected anywhere is an immediate defect (duplication); then E2.2c applies

E2.2c_thin_stratum.test: Detects the plan's 'a stratum is empty' condition, made reachable. 'Empty' is unreachable (smallest n_h=734; rarest N_h=32229, 64x the floor).

conditions.relative: a stratum trips if BOTH its drop rate >= 3x the corpus-wide drop rate AND it loses >= 2% of its allocation

number_provenance.500: reuses #42's max(500, 1%*budget) floor, retained as a non-binding clamp documented structurally inert (smallest Neyman share 1.47% > 1%). If attrition pushes a stratum under 500, that inert clamp becomes retroactively binding — the event worth naming.
number_provenance.3x_and_2pct: judgement calls, not derivations. Defensible against #50's near-zero attrition expectation (C1's always-full-res scoring means the catalog's land_std/exact_zero_frac were computed on the same array E1 reads). Conjunction required: a pure ratio detonates on small denominators; the 2% floor (15 windows for the smallest stratum) stops noise from firing.

backfill_to_budget.rationale: A miss means the backfill rule failed.

accept_shortfall.test: realized_coastal / realized_total >= 0.01337 (the frame rate, not the count)
accept_shortfall.rationale: 670 is a RATE wearing a count's clothes: #42 derived it as coastline's within-frame rate (40,815/3,052,735 = 1.337%; 670/50,000 = 1.340%). If the denominator shrinks, honoring the count would OVER-represent coast; honoring the rate is correct. The realized count is reported in the corpus card as itself, never rounded up to 670, never described as 'met'. A breach means enforce-by-construction at selection does not survive materialization — a design change (select coastal with margin), hence a Finding.
accept_shortfall.exposure_note: Coastline windows are by construction high-zero-fraction — precisely the population most exposed to normalize.py's zero-fill re-screen, so this criterion has real teeth.

E2.3_coverage.test: Per-geo-cell count map + table. Diagnostic: shows WHERE the corpus landed, and is the figure behind the E3 note on deliberate geo-non-uniformity.
E2.3_coverage.explicitly_never_a_gate: Any geographic pass condition smuggles geo-uniformity back in, fighting Neyman. A floor-per-cell would force tiles into terrain-redundant cells. A 50k draw over 15,834 COGs (mean 3.16 windows/COG) cannot touch all cells; 'coverage floor' has no reachable value. The 47 hollow cells (#36) are a kept-frame fact, not a corpus prediction.

guard.test: no single COG exceeds 64 windows in the materialized corpus
guard.number_provenance: reuses #42's retired ADR-0001-era per-COG cap of 64 (retired as inert at debug tier: ~2 windows/COG). As a tripwire it never fires on a healthy corpus (measured max 44, p99 16, mean 3.16); it only fires if materialization concentrated windows in a way selection never intended (broken round-robin, looping COG read, collapsed stratum).

E2.4_gallery_coherence.form: human protocol, not code — see docs/research/e2-gallery-protocol.md
E2.4_gallery_coherence.test: Per stratum, reviewer marks coherent / mixed / incoherent (do the 12 tiles read as variations on one terrain theme?).
E2.4_gallery_coherence.fail_condition: any stratum marked incoherent, OR >= 3 strata marked mixed
E2.4_gallery_coherence.disavowed: Distinguishability (can you tell stratum A from B?) is NOT the gate. #41 found the descriptor space is a continuum, not clumps; adjacent strata blending is expected. A correct k=20 partition of a continuum would fail a distinguishability gate.
E2.4_gallery_coherence.naming_prompt: Reviewer writes a terrain-family label per stratum. Recorded, not gated — some strata won't have a clean folk name and that's fine. Seeds E3 and ADR-0005 stratum descriptions; feeds the coherence call.
E2.4_gallery_coherence.falsification: The strata are falsified when the terrain partition is not visually recoverable — a stratum whose members share no terrain theme (incoherent), or enough mixed strata that the partition reads as noise. NOT when neighbours resemble each other.
E2.4_gallery_coherence.fallback: plan risk #2 — the published Iwahashi 40-cluster global product as an external stratum label (a fresh map, not a repair here)

E2.5_gate_attrition_bias.build_method: retroactive centroid assignment — the 1,333,985 dropped windows are still in the catalog (#37: gates are columns) with full metrics but no stratum_id (k-means was fit on survivors only). Score each dropped window against the committed centroids.json + scaler.json to give it the stratum it WOULD have joined, then tabulate drops per (gate x stratum).
E2.5_gate_attrition_bias.set_blind: This Phase-C half of the table is computable TODAY from committed artifacts (catalog x centroids), so it contains no Phase E information. Its threshold is therefore set BLIND, on principle, and the table is NOT computed until #52 runs. Peeking first would be rationalization, not pre-registration.
E2.5_gate_attrition_bias.test: For each (gate x stratum) pair, fire if BOTH: the gate's within-stratum drop rate >= 3x that same gate's corpus-wide drop rate, AND that gate removes >= 10% of the stratum's would-be (pre-gate) membership.

number_provenance.shape: conjunction, same as E2.2c: 3x catches concentration, the absolute floor insists the bite is substantial
number_provenance.10pct_not_2pct: thinness (E2.2c) is about starvation, where 2% matters; HOLLOWING is a claim about a gate taking a big bite of a terrain family. #36 showed EDM can take >50% of an extreme band, so 10% is where 'hollowed' is honestly the right word.
number_provenance.baseline: #36 checked per-geo-cell and per-band and cleared risk #3 ('families and bands all survive'), but could not check per-STRATUM (strata didn't exist yet). E2.5 is the first per-stratum look; the pre-registered expectation is even attrition, so a firing is a genuine surprise.

E2.5_gate_attrition_bias.implicated_knob: WBM water cap OR EDM/FLM cap (whichever gate fired)
E2.5_gate_attrition_bias.graduates_fog: A firing graduates the map's 'per-stratum quality-gate loosening' fog (Not yet specified) into a fresh map targeting the specific (gate, stratum). Does NOT re-open the global thresholds (Out of scope). If even, the fog 'may graduate into nothing' — recorded here.
E2.5_gate_attrition_bias.materialization_column: The published table also shows #50 materialization drops as an additional column beside the Phase-C gates (one place for both attritions, per #50 item 4), but only the Phase-C gate-bias question carries the 3x/10% gate. The materialization-attrition count effect is covered by E2.2c and its metric-selectivity by E2.1b.

finding_payload_schema.note: Every Finding carries exactly these four fields, emitted mechanically by #52 so the handoff to a fresh map is usable. A Finding names the knob; it does NOT prescribe the new value — that is the fresh map's call.

fields.implicated_knob: named from the plan §215-228 knob table verbatim (the criterion's pre-assigned knob above). If a criterion can't name a knob from the table, it is a Defect, not a Finding.
fields.measured_miss: the statistic and the threshold it crossed, as numbers (e.g. 'stratum 13: EDM within-stratum drop 34%, corpus-wide 6%, ratio 5.7x, absolute loss 22%')
fields.evidence_pointer: committed figure/table + notebook cell by path (the manifest Parquet + report under docs/research/ — the corpus shards are gitignored)
fields.class: Defect or Finding restated; a Defect payload additionally names the suspected code path

verdict_rollup.note: Pre-registered aggregation rule. Emitted by #54 into the E2 report and posted as the resolution comment on the map (#46). This ticket pins the SHAPE; #54 fills the form.

state_machine.consequence: fix, re-run E1/E2, STAY IN MAP; not a Gate E verdict. Finding-level criteria are reported but marked not-yet-adjudicated (cannot judge the design from a corpus known to be mis-built).
record verdict + payloads, STOP, fresh map. No partial credit — the analyses test different failure modes; one firing is one real design flaw.
E3 honesty notes (#55) and ADR-0005 (#56) proceed.

verdict_rollup.rationale: Leaf thresholds are hard to fudge once they're numbers in a committed file; 'on balance it's basically fine' is easy to fudge — unless the rule that turns leaves into a verdict was itself written before the leaves had values.
